page.title: Settings
page.purpose: Show how this scenario is configured: which providers are available, whether their credentials resolve, and how often the reconciler and expiry sweeper run.

priorities.statement: Which providers are configured and whether each can actually be reached.
That credentials resolve, without ever displaying one.
Each provider's billing facts, because product decisions depend on them.
How often the unattended loops run.

states.description: Configured providers with credential status and billing facts.
No provider is configured, so nothing can be provisioned. The page says exactly that.
Providers render but at least one credential status could not be checked, shown as unknown rather than as healthy.
Sweep completion times are older than their interval, which is itself the signal that a loop has stopped.

elements.name: Provider
elements.description: Identifier, credential status, and declared billing facts.

elements.name: Billing facts
elements.description: Rounding, minimum billable unit, whether a stopped instance bills, and whether inbound traffic is charged.

elements.name: Sweep intervals
elements.description: Reconciler and expiry sweeper schedules, and when each last completed.

claims.statement: No credential value is rendered anywhere on this page, in any state, including a masked or partial form.
claims.rationale: Provider tokens resolve through the credential authority at call time. A masked secret in a UI is still a secret in a screenshot.

claims.statement: Each provider's rounding, minimum billable unit and stopped-instance behaviour are shown as data rather than buried in documentation.
claims.rationale: These constants decide whether a short-lived instance is profitable. They belong where the operator can see them.

claims.statement: With no provider configured, the page states that nothing can be provisioned rather than rendering an empty list.
Every declared state renders a distinct, readable surface.
